messages:
charlie_customer: Hey, hitting a weird 400 from the embeddings endpoint when we send batched vectors from our frontend. Works for single-item calls but fails when we send a batch of 8. Response says "dimension mismatch". Anyone seen this?

alice_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request body + headers (curl or fetch) and the full 400 response body? Often this is a client-side encoding issue (strings vs arrays) or content-type.

charlie_customer: Here you go — this is what the frontend is sending (using fetch):
```
fetch('https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $TOKEN' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'text-embedding-3-small', input: "[[0.12, 0.3, ... 0.07],[ ... ]]" })
})
```
And the API returns: `{"error":"Bad Request","message":"embedding vector length 1 != expected 1536"}`

alice_support: Ah — looks like the input field is a stringified JSON array (note the quotes around the whole vector array). That will be parsed by the server as a single scalar string, so validation sees a string length / token count mismatch rather than an array of numbers. Also I don't see Content-Type: application/json in the headers — some browsers default to text/plain for fetch body if header omitted. Two issues to fix: remove the extra quoting and set the header.

charlie_customer: omg, that was the bug. We were double-stringifying in our helper. Quick question: why does single-item call succeed?

maria_engineering: Single-item often passes because the server accepts a scalar string (it can attempt to coerce small inputs or the embedding service gives a default embedding path), but for batched calls the schema validator strictly expects an array-of-arrays of floats. Also when dimension checks run they see a single string token rather than a numeric vector and report the mismatch.

alice_support: Steps to repro & fix we recommend: 1) ensure Content-Type header is set: `Content-Type: application/json` 2) pass native JS arrays — do NOT JSON.stringify the inner array again. Example working curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":[[0.12,0.3,0.07,...],[0.05,0.14,0.22,...]]}'
```
Replace ellipses with full 1536-length vectors for the model.

embed-bot: validation.log: request_id=rq_9e8f3 | status=400 | reason="input is string, expected array" | route=/v1/embeddings | user=acct-123

charlie_customer: After changing that and adding Content-Type it stopped returning 400. Thanks! One more: our throughput dropped a lot when we switched from batching 8 to 64 — any tips?

maria_engineering: For throughput: 1) avoid very uneven batches in the same request stream — mixing tiny and huge batches can cause dynamic batching to underperform. 2) use consistent batch_size (we recommend 8–16 for low latency or 64–128 for high throughput depending on model). 3) enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes. 4) if you need high throughput with low unit cost, consider quantized model variant and Dedicated capacity.

alice_support: Also watch for hidden serialization work: if you pre-serialize to strings accidentally, it adds CPU and increases latency. If you see billing spikes after fixing this, ping us — we can trace request_ids.

charlie_customer: Noted. Appreciate the detailed help — we'll roll the fix to prod and monitor. :thumbsup:

alice_support: Great — if you hit anything else paste the failing request_id and we can pull the logs (e.g., rq_9e8f3). Closing for now but reopen if it recurs. :wave:
